newsitem.title: FRANCE: New bomb attack in Corsica - no one hurt.
newsitem.headline: New bomb attack in Corsica - no one hurt.

text.p: A small bomb exploded on the troubled French Mediterranean island of Corsica on Friday in the 20th attempt to damage post offices in only a month.

Police said no one was hurt and there was only slight damage when the charge went off outside the post office shortly after midnight in the small town of Folelli. They did not know who the attackers were.
Post offices, often the only symbol in rural Corsican areas of the central government in Paris, are frequent targets of militant nationalists who seek to loosen ties with the mainland.
Police said last month they had arrested two young men who confessed to carrying out six such attacks in recent weeks. The two are now in a Paris prison awaiting trial.
There were conflicting calls for war and peace on the island after Prime Minister Alain Juppe vowed to crush separatists who bombed his mayoral office in Bordeaux at the weekend.

The separatist group Fronte Ribellu (Rebel Front) called on the 250,000 islanders to rise up against French "aggressors", it branded "the hereditary enemy" in a statement sent to a news agency in Bastia.
It threatened to kill anyone who assisted police in the crackdown promised by Juppe against the separatists.
